article.headline: Tencent Open-Sources a World Model That Outputs Real 3D Assets
article.lede: The gap between world models that look impressive in demos and those you can actually ship has been the field’s quiet embarrassment. Tencent’s HY-World 2.0, released in April 2026 as a fully open-source project, claims to close it: a multi-modal pipeline that converts text, images, or video into editable, production-ready 3D assets importable directly into Unreal Engine, Unity, and Blender. Where rival approaches generate video that cannot be exported or modified, HY-World 2.0 produces persistent geometry—the kind that behaves like any other 3D asset in a production pipeline.
article.body:
**Tencent** (0700.HK) has spent the past year building toward a deceptively simple promise: a world model whose output you can actually import into a game engine. HY-World 2.0 is a multi-modal pipeline that accepts text, still images, multi-view photos, or video and produces *3D Gaussian Splatting* scenes—a representation that encodes a 3D space as millions of tiny calibrated splats rather than solid polygons—paired with conventional meshes, point clouds, depth maps, and calibrated camera parameters, all in a single inference pass.

The distinction matters because the world-model field has quietly split into two camps. Video-streaming approaches—Google DeepMind (GOOGL)’s Genie 3, along with offerings from Meta (META) and assorted startups—generate interactive environments as continuous video frames. Impressive in demos, but fundamentally ephemeral: you cannot export the geometry, edit individual objects, or import the result into a production pipeline. HY-World 2.0 sits in the second, smaller camp alongside World Labs’ *Marble*—the closed-source system from Fei-Fei Li’s company—that treats the generated world as persistent, editable geometry rather than a movie.

The currently released component is WorldMirror 2.0, a roughly 1.2-billion-parameter *feed-forward reconstruction* model—meaning it predicts the full 3D structure in one pass rather than iterating through a slow optimisation loop, as early *NeRF* (Neural Radiance Field) methods did. Technical novelties include a Normalized *RoPE* position-encoding scheme that maps spatial coordinates to a fixed range, letting the model generalise across image resolutions without retraining. A companion rendering layer called WorldLens converts raw model outputs into engine-agnostic assets, baking in automatic *image-based lighting* and collision geometry before export.

The “character mode” is the most immediately legible proof of the production claim. Rather than delivering a frozen scene file, HY-World 2.0 lets a developer walk through the generated environment in real time with physics-accurate collision detection active—a built-in playtest loop that catches spatial errors before the asset ever touches an engine. The team benchmarks WorldMirror 2.0 as state-of-the-art among open-source systems and comparable to Marble on standard geometric reconstruction datasets; neither claim has been independently replicated, though the accompanying arXiv paper (2604.14268) provides evaluation detail. Three of the four advertised pipeline components—HY-Pano 2.0, WorldNav, and WorldStereo 2.0—are listed as coming soon, meaning what is available today is one quarter of the full system. Nvidia (NVDA) Cosmos, often invoked alongside these projects, operates in a different lane: robotics and autonomous-vehicle synthetic-data generation via physics-aware video diffusion, not game-ready geometry.

Tencent’s motivation is not purely altruistic. The company operates *Honor of Kings* and *PUBG Mobile*, two of the world’s highest-revenue mobile titles, giving it direct incentive to compress the weeks of specialised 3D modelling that world-building currently requires. Open-sourcing the model seeds an ecosystem of tooling and fine-tunes that a proprietary release could not, while Tencent Cloud and the Hunyuan 3D Creation Engine platform provide the obvious commercial on-ramp. Whether the remaining pipeline modules arrive on schedule—and whether independent benchmarks validate the Marble-parity claim—will determine whether HY-World 2.0 becomes infrastructure or another impressive demo.

concepts.definition: An AI system that builds an internal representation of an environment—its geometry, physics, and dynamics—rather than simply generating images or video. World models can be queried or explored interactively, and their outputs may persist as navigable, editable scenes rather than ephemeral pixels.

A method of representing 3D scenes as millions of tiny oriented ellipsoids (Gaussian splats) placed in space, each encoding colour and opacity. Unlike polygonal meshes, which define hard surfaces, Gaussian Splatting captures complex visual detail and renders in real time. Outputs can be paired with conventional meshes for physics simulation and engine import.

An approach to 3D scene reconstruction in which a neural network predicts the complete 3D structure from input images in a single forward pass, rather than iterating through a slow per-scene optimisation loop. Much faster at inference time, but performance depends heavily on the breadth of training data.

Neural Radiance Field—a technique that represents a 3D scene as a continuous function learned by a neural network, mapping any 3D position and viewing direction to colour and density. Introduced in 2020, NeRFs produce photorealistic novel views but require slow per-scene optimisation, a limitation that feed-forward and Gaussian Splatting methods have largely supplanted.

Rotary Position Encoding—a method of injecting positional information into transformer attention layers by rotating query and key vectors. Originally developed for language models, it has been adapted for spatial coordinates in vision systems. The “Normalized” variant in HY-World 2.0 maps all spatial positions to a fixed range, enabling generalisation across image resolutions without retraining.

A rendering technique that uses a photograph of a real environment—typically a 360-degree HDR image—to illuminate a 3D scene realistically. Automatically inferring appropriate lighting from generated scene data is a non-trivial step that makes exported assets look plausible under real-world conditions without manual artist intervention.

repos.summary: The official open-source release of HY-World 2.0, currently containing WorldMirror 2.0 code and pretrained weights (approximately 1.2 billion parameters) for feed-forward 3D reconstruction. Users provide text, image, or video inputs and receive 3DGS scenes, meshes, point clouds, depth maps, and camera parameters in one inference pass; single-GPU and multi-GPU FSDP inference in BF16 precision are both supported. The remaining pipeline components—HY-Pano 2.0, WorldNav, and WorldStereo 2.0—are listed as coming soon.

article.fact_check: The announcement presents HY-World 2.0 as a complete, production-ready system, but only one of its four advertised pipeline modules (WorldMirror 2.0) is currently released; the other three are listed as “coming soon.” The claim of parity with World Labs’ Marble is drawn from the team’s own arXiv paper rather than independent benchmarking, and should be treated as self-reported until third parties replicate the evaluation.

ticker_0700-hk.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
ticker_0700-hk.blurb: Tencent Holdings Limited is an investment holding company that provides value-added services, marketing services, fintech, and business services in Mainland China and internationally. Its consumer business includes communications and social services (instant messaging and social networks), digital content (online games, videos, live streaming, news, music, and literature), fintech services (mobile payment, wealth management, consumer loans, and securities trading), and various tools. Tencent is one of the world's largest internet and technology companies by revenue and market capitalization, with a dominant position in China's social media and gaming markets.
ticker_0700-hk.recent: In the past 30 days, Tencent's stock price has shown volatility, trading in a range of approximately 460 to 480 HKD. The company is scheduled to report earnings on May 13, 2026, with analysts expecting continued revenue growth driven by its fintech and gaming segments. Recent news highlights include regulatory developments in China's tech sector and Tencent's ongoing investments in AI and cloud computing.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_meta.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
ticker_meta.blurb: Meta Platforms, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads — collectively the largest social-media ecosystem in the world by monthly active users. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue through digital advertising, using detailed behavioural data to target ads across its platforms. After a painful 2022 in which shares fell roughly 65% amid a revenue slowdown and ballooning metaverse losses, Meta executed a dramatic turnaround by cutting costs, boosting margins, and rapidly integrating AI-driven ad ranking tools (Advantage+) that demonstrably improved advertiser returns. CEO Mark Zuckerberg declared 2023 a 'Year of Efficiency' and the company followed through. By late 2025 Meta was simultaneously the most profitable it had ever been and the most aggressive in AI infrastructure spending, committing up to $65 billion in capex for 2025 and raising that figure to as much as $145 billion for 2026.
ticker_meta.recent: Meta reached an all-time high near $796 per share in September 2025. The stock declined approximately 24–28% from that peak through April 2026, with the primary investor concern being the scale of the 2026 capital-expenditure commitment — up to $145 billion — and uncertainty about whether AI-driven revenue would materialise at the pace required to justify it. Quarterly earnings remained strong through the period, but multiple compression drove share-price weakness.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.
